It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where political powers grow cold toward the Gospel and seek to claim authority that belongs to the King alone, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the boundaries between Caesar and the Savior in this hour? [13, 243, 252, 1331, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who use human law as a “scourge” against the faithful, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “history is His story”—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory where “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [13, 20, 92, 263, 1143, 1283, 1301, 1405, 1425, 1471, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many seek “diplomatic relations” with the culture to avoid the “scars” of the cross, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by reminding us that our “citizenship is in heaven” [11, 15, 19, 21, 26, 28, 38, 41, 132, 1197, 1313, 1316, 1320, 1326, 1426, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur** and **John Calvin**—teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, a state’s claim over the church's worship is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” [15, 68, 208, 250, 671, 1143, 1392, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: Christ’s Exclusive Headship**

**Verse**
“And He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things He may have the preeminence” (Colossians 1:18). [255, 293, 617, 1429, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scripture declares that “He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things He may have the preeminence” (Colossians 1:18). [255, 293, 617, 1429, Conversation History]. Christ alone is the sovereign Master of His people, for the Father “put all things under His feet, and gave Him to be head over all things to the church, which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all” (Ephesians 1:22–23). [255, 1099, 1101, 1426, Conversation History]. This means that the church's “sole objective” is to follow the One who “highly exalted Him and given Him the name which is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, and of those on earth, and of those under the earth, and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father” (Philippians 2:9–11). [257, 258, 291, 784, 889, 906, 1426, Conversation History]. Because “He is the radiance of His [Father’s] glory and the exact representation of His nature, and upholds all things by the word of His power,” no human ruler can rightfully govern the internal affairs of the redeemed (Hebrews 1:3). [13, 31, 42, 616, 1315, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by “worldly philosophy” that suggests any earthly leader can claim Christ's title, for “no slave can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other” (Matthew 6:24). [170, 327, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that “the Lord has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all” (Psalm 103:19). [42, 68, 318, 1143, 1515, 1532, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the religious leaders of the Sanhedrin often acted as a “religious court,” yet they were exposed as “usurpers” when they rejected the Word of the Lord to maintain their “political status,” for Jesus warned, “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith” (Matthew 23:23). [174, 180, 204, 1091, 1316, 1422, 1720, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our worship, showing that “God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth,” which means the church's validity comes from Christ's Word, not a “formal license” from a “governor” (John 4:24). [13, 17, 23, 30, 31, 142, 412, 415, 888, 1313, 1426, 1445, 1529, 1611, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

### **Section 2: The Ordained Role of the State**

**Verse**
“Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God” (Romans 13:1). [75, 892, 902, 1016, 1184, 1202, 1246, 1284, 1342, 1422, 1473, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Believers are commanded to be “loyal and submissive” to civil government, for “whoever resists the authority resists the ordinance of God, and those who resist will bring judgment on themselves” (Romans 13:2). [15, 18, 52, 75, 76, 78, 1143, 1342, 1422, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. The state is “God’s minister to you for good,” intended to “retard the corruption” of society and maintain order, as Peter instructed: “Therefore submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake, whether to the king as supreme, or to governors, as to those who are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do good” (1 Peter 2:13–14). [15, 18, 29, 75, 76, 78, 892, 893, 1017, 1042, 1143, 1184, 1284, 1422, 1473, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. However, we recognize that “the judgment is God’s,” and therefore the magistrate’s power is limited to secular and moral spheres, not the sanctuary of the conscience (Deuteronomy 1:17). [11, 37, 79, 131, 136, 1023, 1235, 1321, 1332, 1343, 1406, 1473, 1503, 1709, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity” by obeying civil laws in all things that do not violate God's law, for “this is the will of God, that by doing good you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men” (1 Timothy 2:2; 1 Peter 2:15). [21, 76, 79, 82, 93, 116, 893, 925, 1017, 1105, 1284, 1473, 1709, Conversation History]. “Honor all people. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king” (1 Peter 2:17). [15, 39, 47, 68, 75, 87, 116, 926, 1017, 1106, 1143, 1181, 1202, 1214, 1406, 1502, 1532, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Theocracy vs. Pilgrimage**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national greatness” was often a “temporal sign” of favor, yet God “removed kings” who “rejected the word of the LORD,” as when Samuel told Saul, “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, As in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, And to heed than the fat of rams” (1 Samuel 15:22). [15, 17, 18, 409, 882, 1078, 1183, 1313, 1353, 1519, 1533, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our view, showing that we are “sojourners and pilgrims” whose “citizenship is in heaven,” and therefore our ultimate allegiance is to the King who said, “My kingdom is not of this world” (1 Peter 2:11; Philippians 3:20; John 18:36). [13, 21, 26, 28, 29, 38, 142, 440, 1023, 1203, 1313, 1320, 1326, 1330, 1426, 1529, Conversation History].

### **Section 3: Resistance to Civil Usurpation**

**Verse**
“But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: ‘We ought to obey God rather than men. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus whom you murdered by hanging on a tree’ ” (Acts 5:29–30). [48, 875, 914, 1078, 1130, 1164, 1176, 1205, 1247, 1249, 1256, 1300, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
When the state forbids what God commands—such as the “binding and authoritative mandate” to preach the gospel—the church must “refuse to yield submission,” for “we ought to obey God rather than men” (Acts 5:29). [11, 15, 19, 1130, 1144, 1176, 1205, 1217, 1247, 1256, 1300, 1316, 1370, 1431, 1500, 1503, 1528, 1529, 1545, 1636, 1638, 1720, Conversation History]. Christ warned that “a servant is not greater than his master. If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you,” and in such times, we must “not be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do” (John 15:20; Luke 12:4). [53, 219, 239, 266, 282, 301, 331, 332, 617, 655, 744, 795, 819, 893, 923, 936, 942, 980, 1056, 1313, 1316, 1378, 1403, 1404, 1513, 1515, 1596, 1672, Conversation History]. Even if a state “makes havoc of the church,” the “word of God is not chained” and will outlast its enemies, for “heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away” (Matthew 24:35; 2 Timothy 2:9). [11, 25, 41, 123, 1198, 1204, 1211, 1241, 1268, 1283, 1306, 1314, 1316, 1420, 1504, 1515, 1646, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict,” refusing to let human laws “tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel” (1 Thessalonians 2:2; Galatians 2:5). [51, 76, 91, 1081, 1083, 1406, 1431, 1461, 1503, 1670, Conversation History]. “Contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints,” for “your life is not your own” because “you were bought at a price” (Jude 3; 1 Corinthians 6:19–20). [11, 12, 21, 92, 99, 101, 113, 201, 212, 237, 238, 265, 361, 629, 750, 760, 772, 833, 873, 932, 1066, 1132, 1137, 1138, 1141, 1242, 1246, 1262, 1312, 1334, 1358, 1389, 1406, 1408, 1440, 1442, 1451, 1461, 1463, 1503, 1515, 1572, 1601, 1670, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, God used “hostile nations” as the “rod of My anger” to judge unfaithfulness, as Isaiah wrote, “Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger and the staff in whose hand is My indignation” (Isaiah 10:5). [717, 740, 847, 924, 1110, 1130, 1133, 1316, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” showing that the “church militant” conquers not by the sword but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” for our “victory that has overcome the world” is “our faith” (Revelation 12:11; 1 John 5:4). [13, 21, 32, 92, 1113, 1313, 1402, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

### **Section 4: The Final Reckoning for the Despot**

**Verse**
“Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [103, 133, 158, 174, 650, 1199, 1315, 1524, 1636, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals that human “monuments to their pride” and “storage cities” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away,” but “the Word of our God stands forever” (Psalm 102:3; Isaiah 40:8). [11, 32, 35, 37, 39, 43, 63, 789, 836, 940, 976, 1211, 1233, 1241, 1306, 1315, 1408, 1460, 1684, Conversation History]. Christ will ultimately “judge between the nations,” and every ruler who “wrote themselves into God’s office” will be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Isaiah 2:4; Daniel 5:27). [11, 15, 30, 32, 35, 37, 39, 63, 210, 412, 452, 470, 717, 789, 818, 825, 827, 855, 867, 869, 903, 912, 917, 940, 947, 952, 958, 976, 1004, 1061, 1113, 1143, 1183, 1233, 1259, 1260, 1266, 1268, 1288, 1290, 1300, 1301, 1315, 1402, 1408, 1450, 1460, 1473, 1502, 1515, 1519, 1684, 1720, Conversation History]. On that Day, the “church triumphant” will find an “inheritance incorruptible and undefiled” where “God will wipe away every tear from their eyes” (1 Peter 1:4; Revelation 21:4). [13, 14, 21, 24, 26, 31, 32, 38, 92, 94, 109, 121, 142, 152, 190, 192, 201, 243, 301, 321, 331, 332, 333, 334, 337, 339, 352, 442, 470, 719, 730, 816, 822, 830, 903, 948, 1009, 1016, 1020, 1033, 1039, 1128, 1132, 1143, 1162, 1197, 1203, 1251, 1255, 1257, 1259, 1282, 1313, 1315, 1316, 1320, 1321, 1326, 1342, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1503, 1515, 1529, 1563, 1646, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the Lord knows those who are His” and His “everlasting dominion” is the only kingdom that “shall not pass away” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 2 Timothy 2:19; Daniel 7:14). [11, 24, 47, 87, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 211, 222, 266, 273, 278, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 352, 361, 386, 405, 412, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 602, 614, 630, 788, 852, 869, 921, 957, 958, 1035, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1183, 1300, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1315, 1407, 1408, 1420, 1441, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History]. Find “tranquility of soul” by resting upon the “surest foundation,” for “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6). “Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). The law’s demands and threats are relentless. “Whoever shall keep the whole law, and yet stumble in one point, he is guilty of all” (James 2:10). And what you actually see here in Matthew 10 is the very beginning of the process that is described in Hebrews 2, verses 3 and 4. Which tells us that the gospel was at first declared by the Lord, and it was attested to us by those who heard while God also bore witness by signs and wonders and various miracles and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will. And these uniquely miraculous gifts are referred to in 2 Corinthians 12:12 as the signs of a true Apostle, signs and wonders and mighty works. So Paul is saying in 1 Corinthians 12 that the very essence of what made the Apostles unique was their ability to speak infallibly with God's own authority and then to validate that message with signs and wonders and mighty works. Earlier He told the crowds who flocked to hear Him, “If you continue in My word, then you are truly disciples of Mine” (John 8:31); and elsewhere: “If anyone wishes to come after Me, he must deny himself, and take up his cross daily and follow Me” (Luke 9:23; cf. the people for His own possession.7 We are those who belong to Him, not because we chose Him but because He chose us. But unlike the Roman slave market—where slaves were selected based on their positive qualities, like strength, health, and physical appearance—God chose His slaves with the full knowledge of their weaknesses and failures. We “were not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble; but God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God has chosen the weak things of the world to shame the things which are strong” (1 Cor. 1:26–27). Indeed, He mercifully elected us to salvation in spite of ourselves, saving us—not because of any inherent goodness in us—but according to His own eternal purposes and for the sake of His glory.

Having delivered us from the destitution of sin, God not only receives us as His slaves—but He has also welcomed us into His household and made us members of His very family. He not only rescued us, purchased us, befriended us, and took us in; He has also adopted us, thereby transforming those who were formerly children of wrath (Eph. 2:3) into the sons and daughters of righteousness. All of this is possible through the redemptive work of Christ, who is the “only begotten Son” (John 3:16), and the “firstborn among many brethren” (Rom. 8:29; cf. Rev. 1:5).13

The term firstborn, when applied to Jesus Christ, does not imply that He was created (as some cult groups claim). Rather, in both Jewish and Greco-Roman culture, the “firstborn” was the ranking son who was given the right of inheritance, whether he was born first or not. Thus, the title “firstborn” means “highest ranking” or “preeminent.” 14. For a discussion as to why Roman, rather than Greek, law is behind much of the New Testament’s adoption language, see Francis Lyall, Slaves, Citizens, Sons: Legal Metaphors in the Epistles (Grand Rapids: Academie Books, 1984), 95–99. 15. Cf. Lyall, Slaves, Citizens, Sons, 125–26. Though adoption, in general, was fairly common, the formal adoption of slaves, in particular, was much rarer. Informally, any manumitted slave would view his former master—namely, the one who set him free—as a father figure or patron (cf. James S. Jeffers, The Greco-Roman World of the New Testament [Downers Grove, IL: InterVarsity Press, 1999], 239). Because God set us free from slavery to sin, this analogy could also apply to the believer. However, the New Testament language of adoption assumes the formal legal process, in which the full privileges of sonship and an inheritance are officially bestowed.

In other words, the family relationships from which ancient communities and villages—and eventually towns, cities, and nations— emerged, cemented the loyalty of the citizens to their homeland and to their fellow countrymen. To be a citizen was, in a very real sense, to be part of an extended family. The Parallel to Heavenly Citizenship The imagery of citizenship conveys a number of important truths about the Christian life—especially in light of first-century slavery and manumission. Having been redeemed by Christ and empowered by the Holy Spirit, believers have everything they need to gain victory over temptation and sin. The power of sin has been permanently broken. The condemnation of the Law has been forever removed. The freedom of obedience is ours to possess. Now “we serve in newness of the Spirit” (Rom. 7:6). In being Christ’s slaves, we are finally and fully liberated; in submitting to Him we experience true emancipation, for His law has forever set us free from the law of sin and death (Rom. 8:2).
